properties.decision:
Anthony, 2026-08-26, accepting a ruling the agent drafted and put to him with its alternative. The last two of the thirty-three leaf parts `unallocated_component` reported as holding no function: `cmp:memory-backend` and `cmp:rocksdb-backend`.

═══ WHAT THEY ARE ═══

They are the two interchangeable implementations behind `ifc:kv-backend`, both PROVIDES, sitting under `cmp:byte-store`. Neither carries an Artifact, because neither is one file. `cap:store` — "schema-validated graph store" — is already allocated to `cmp:schema`, `cmp:byte-store` and `cmp:nodes`.

═══ THE RULING ═══

**An interchangeable implementation is named by the contract it satisfies, not by a function of its own.** Both backends already say what they are for, in the design's own vocabulary: they PROVIDE `ifc:kv-backend`. Neither adds a capability the other lacks — that is what makes them swappable, and the whole point of the interface.

The alternative was to allocate `cap:store` to both. Declined: it would put one capability on five components, at which point the WHAT→WHERE binding stops binding anything and says only "somewhere in the storage subsystem". Schema validation is not what a byte backend does.

═══ WHOSE WORD THIS IS ═══

⚠️ **THE REASONING IS THE AGENT'S; THE ACCEPTANCE IS THE OWNER'S, AND THE TWO ARE RECORDED SEPARATELY ON PURPOSE.** It was drafted on 2026-08-25 from the session's own reading, deliberately left `proposed` overnight rather than accepted on his behalf, and put to him as an open question alongside the finished work. He accepted it on 2026-08-26 without amendment.

That distinction is the same one `dec:idea-a-user-carries-a-persona-that-shapes-every-reply` says is load-bearing between a SELF-DESCRIBED and an ASSIGNED reading, and it is worth keeping here for the same reason: a later reader asking "did he actually decide this, or did an agent decide it and nobody objected?" gets a straight answer. He did decide it. He did not originate it.

📌 `cmp:rocksdb-backend` is additionally governed by `dec:the-rust-rocksdb-switch-is-parked-until-the-store-question-settles`. That parks the SWITCH between backends; this parks the question of what either one is FOR. Different questions, both live on the same node.
properties.name: DECIDED — the two byte-store backends hold no function of their own: what they are for is the contract they provide
properties.rationale:
Kept separate from the tool-surface ruling because the justification is genuinely different, and one decision covering both would let a later reader apply the wrong reason to the wrong parts. The tool slices are empty because a surface must not hold its subject's function; these two are empty because two implementations of one contract cannot differ in what they are for without ceasing to be interchangeable.

Recorded as a Decision rather than left as an acknowledgement so that the judgement carries its author and its reasoning, and so a structural detector can read the ruling rather than a reviewer having to remember it.
